question: What is the primary goal of safe motherhood initiatives?

options.A: Ensuring healthy pregnancy and childbirth without life-threatening risks
options.B: Eliminating the need for traditional birth attendants completely
options.C: Increasing the national population growth rate rapidly
options.D: Providing free formula milk to every newborn baby

explanation: Safe motherhood focuses directly on protecting women from preventable complications during pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h1)

question: Why is safe motherhood considered a broad public health issue rather than just a clinical concern?

options.A: Only community health extension workers are legally allowed to manage it
options.B: Hospitals in rural areas refuse to admit pregnant women entirely
options.C: Medical doctors do not participate in antenatal care programs
options.D: It involves socio-cultural factors, poverty, and healthcare access barriers

explanation: Maternal health outcomes depend heavily on community dynamics, financial status, and the availability of functional health systems. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h1)

question: Which component is recognized as a core pillar of safe motherhood?
explanation: Antenatal care is one of the foundational pillars designed to monitor and protect maternal health throughout gestation. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h2)

question: How does family planning directly support the principles of safe motherhood?

options.A: By eliminating all genetic disorders before conception occurs
options.B: By guaranteeing that every woman gives birth to twins
options.C: By preventing high-risk pregnancies through proper birth spacing
options.D: By replacing the need for routine postnatal clinic visits

explanation: Spacing pregnancies allows the mother's body to recover fully, significantly lowering maternal and infant risks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h2)

question: What is the recommended minimum number of antenatal contacts for a pregnant woman?
explanation: Current guidelines advocate for at least eight antenatal contacts to ensure timely detection and management of risks. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h3)

question: A healthy pregnant woman at 20 weeks gestation asks why she needs to attend clinic when she feels completely fine. What is your best response?

options.A: The clinic requires attendance so they can update your registration file
options.B: You only need to return if you start bleeding or experience severe pain
options.C: Feeling fine means your baby is growing without any need for medicines
options.D: Routine visits help monitor fetal growth and catch hidden problems early

explanation: Many complications like gestational hypertension develop silently and require routine screening to detect. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h3)

question: What tool is used during labor to monitor progress and detect prolonged labor early?
explanation: The partograph provides a pictorial overview of labor progress to help clinicians spot deviations from normal parameters. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h4)

question: Why is the presence of a skilled birth attendant during delivery so crucial?

options.A: They ensure that traditional birth songs are sung during delivery
options.B: They can quickly identify and manage sudden, life-threatening complications
options.C: They prevent the mother from experiencing any discomfort during contractions
options.D: They guarantee that the baby will be born without any need for checkups

explanation: Skilled birth attendants have the training and tools to manage emergencies like severe bleeding immediately. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h4)

question: When should the very first postnatal check for the mother and newborn take place?

options.A: Only when the baby gets sick
options.D: At the end of the first week

explanation: The first 24 hours carry the highest risk for severe bleeding and newborn instability, necessitating early assessment. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h5)

question: Which maternal condition must a nurse actively monitor for during routine postnatal assessments?
explanation: Postnatal checks prioritize ensuring the uterus is contracting properly to prevent excessive postpartum bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h5)

question: Which service is provided at a Comprehensive EmONC (CEmONC) facility but NOT at a basic center?

options.C: Manual removal of a retained placenta

explanation: Surgical capacity and blood banking distinguish comprehensive emergency obstetric care centers from basic ones. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of categorizing health facilities into EmONC levels?

options.A: To make sure that nurses only work in surgical departments
options.B: To restrict pregnant women from visiting hospitals in urban areas
options.C: To reduce the overall cost of building new clinics in rural zones
options.D: To ensure prompt access to specific life-saving interventions during emergencies

explanation: EmONC categorization guides referral pathways so patients receive the exact level of critical care they require. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h6)

question: What attitude should a nurse consistently demonstrate to promote safe hospital deliveries?

options.B: Frequent absence during critical labor stages
options.C: Authoritarian control over all family decisions
options.D: Strict indifference toward patient cultural beliefs

explanation: Respectful maternity care encourages women to seek facility delivery rather than avoiding formal health systems. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h7)

question: Why is participation in maternal death surveillance important for practicing midwives?

options.A: It guarantees an increase in institutional funding from the government
options.B: It is used primarily to punish staff members who make clinical errors
options.C: It removes the need to document daily patient vital signs
options.D: It helps identify root causes of fatalities to prevent future occurrences

explanation: Reviewing maternal deaths uncovers systemic gaps, allowing healthcare teams to implement corrective measures. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T002#GNS226_U1_T002_h7)
